classification.difficultyReason: Following the referenced three-sided fencing example, express the parallel side using the fencing constraint, form the area quadratic and use symmetry to find and interpret its maximum.

content.prompt:
A farmer has a straight fence along the boundary of his property. He wishes to fence an enclosure for a bull and has enough materials to erect 300 m of fence. What would be the dimensions of the largest possible rectangular paddock, assuming that he uses the existing boundary fence as one of its sides?

Begin with a diagram.

answer.short: $75\text{ m}$ perpendicular to the existing fence by $150\text{ m}$ parallel to it.
answer.worked:
Let $x$ metres be the length of each side perpendicular to the existing fence. The newly fenced side parallel to it is $(300-2x)$ metres, with $0<x<150$.
$$\begin{align*}A&=x(300-2x)\\A&=300x-2x^2.\end{align*}$$
The area graph is a downward-opening parabola with intercepts $x=0$ and $x=150$. Its axis of symmetry is midway between them:
$$\begin{align*}x&=\frac{0+150}{2}\\x&=75.\end{align*}$$
The maximum area therefore occurs when the perpendicular sides are $75\text{ m}$ long. The parallel side is
$$\begin{align*}300-2x&=300-2(75)\\300-2x&=150\text{ m}.\end{align*}$$
The paddock is $75\text{ m}$ by $150\text{ m}$.

spec.description: Solution model showing the existing straight fence as one side of a rectangle and three newly fenced sides, following Example 13.
spec.mathematics: Two perpendicular sides have length x; the third fenced side has length 300-2x. At maximum area x=75.
spec.answerVisibility: Solution only; students draw their own diagram.
